title: Firefox profiles (Snap install)
whyItMatters: Ubuntu ships Firefox as a Snap. The profile inside the Snap tree holds the same history, bookmarks, cookies and saved logins, and is easy to miss because the normal Firefox folder is empty.
source: Ubuntu has shipped Firefox as a Snap since 22.04; the confined profile lives under ~/snap/firefox/common/.mozilla/firefox: https://askubuntu.com/questions/1414757/where-does-firefox-snap-store-the-profiles
notes: Snap keeps per-app data under ~/snap/<name>/<revision|common>; Firefox uses the common slot so profiles survive revisions. On Ubuntu 22.04+ the native ~/.mozilla/firefox folder usually does not exist. Firefox 147 and later may keep new snap profiles under the snap's .config folder, which this rule does not match.

cleanup.exportFirst: In Firefox, export your bookmarks from the Library and your passwords from the logins settings, and keep both files off this computer.
cleanup.signOut: In Firefox, open the account menu and disconnect this browser from sync, so the account keeps the data and this computer stops using it.
steps: Uninstall the Firefox snap from the App Center or with the Snap Store app.
Move the profile folder that holds the file named in the plan to the Trash, then empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: Removes every Firefox profile in the snap folder: history, bookmarks, saved logins, cookies and downloaded files. Nothing stays on this disk.
cleanup.source: Mozilla Support, Profiles - Where Firefox stores your bookmarks, passwords and other user data: https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/profiles-where-firefox-stores-user-data
